Fitness & wellness / Salons & spas

Booked chairs, kept appointments and clients who come back on time

For hair and beauty salons, nail bars, barbershops, day spas and salon chains, we connect the salon software, POS and WhatsApp so clients book the right stylist or therapist for the right length of time, patch tests happen on time, no-shows follow one policy, clients hear when their next service is due, and commissions come from the same records.

The challenge

What makes salons & spas different.

01

Bookings arrive by phone, Instagram DMs, WhatsApp and walk-ins, so the appointment book is never complete and stylists get double-booked.

02

No-shows and late cancellations on long color or spa services leave expensive chair and room time empty.

03

Clients drift to another salon when nobody reminds them that their color, cut or facial is due.

04

Product suggestions depend on who is on shift, and aftercare advice is rarely written down.

05

Commissions on services, packages and retail are disputed at month end.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for salons & spas.

01

Skill and duration-aware booking

Clients choose a service and stylist on WhatsApp, Instagram or the website; bookings read live availability, block the right duration with processing time and rooms, and confirm with an approved template.

02

Reminders, patch tests and no-shows

Reminders with easy rescheduling, prompts to book an allergy alert (patch) test before color services where the product instructions require one, waitlist offers for late gaps, and a standard no-show flow with manager-approved deposit decisions.

03

Rebooking when the next service is due

Intervals per service that stylists can adjust, a rebooking prompt at checkout, and one reminder near the due date with the same stylist's open slots.

04

Aftercare notes and consented product suggestions

The stylist's own aftercare notes after every visit, and the products they recommended only for clients who said yes, using approved descriptions without medical claims.

05

Commission and incentive statements

Running statements for every stylist and therapist from billed services, packages and retail, a query flow with the bill attached, and an owner-approved payout sheet at month end.

06

Reviews and referrals without quotas

The same review invitation for every client, no staff quotas or name-mention scripts, manager-approved replies, and referral rewards that follow published terms.

Book, attend and visitStandard3–5 weeks

Salon booking, reminders and no-show handling

Book the right service with the right stylist or therapist for the right length of time, send reminders and patch test prompts, fill late gaps from a waitlist, and handle no-shows with one clear policy.

Salons & spas

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Salons take bookings by phone, Instagram, WhatsApp and walk-in. Service length varies by stylist and hair length, color needs processing time, spa treatments need a room and a trained therapist, and color clients may need an allergy alert (patch) test first. No-shows on long services leave expensive gaps, and deposit rules change with each receptionist.

Trigger

A booking request on WhatsApp, Instagram or the website, a change in the appointment book, or an appointment reaching a reminder or no-show checkpoint.

How it runs

  • AI maps free-text requests on WhatsApp or Instagram to a service, and unclear ones go to reception. The booking is matched to stylists or therapists trained for it, using durations, processing time and rooms.
  • Offer real open slots, confirm with an approved template, and send a deposit link for long or high-value services where the salon's policy asks for one.
  • For color services, check the client card for a recent patch test and prompt the client to book one ahead of the visit where the product instructions require it.
  • Send reminders before the appointment with easy reschedule and cancel options.
  • Offer late cancellations to clients waitlisted for that service and stylist.
  • Mark no-shows, send a polite message with the policy, and queue deposit or fee decisions for the manager.

Human checkpoint

The salon manager approves every deposit retention, fee and booking restriction. Stylists check patch test results in person and decide whether a service goes ahead. Anyone reporting a reaction is told to stop and seek medical advice, and the manager is alerted.

Book, attend and visitStarter2–4 weeks

Stylist and therapist commission and incentive statements

Calculate commissions and incentives on services, packages and retail from the salon's own billing records, show each stylist or therapist a running statement, and give the owner a reviewed payout sheet at month end.

Salons & spas

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Salon pay usually mixes a fixed salary with commission on services, different rates for color, chemical and spa work, package redemptions, retail sales and targets. When the calculation lives in spreadsheets, staff cannot see where they stand, discounts and redos are treated inconsistently, and month end becomes a dispute.

Trigger

Each completed and billed service or retail sale, plus the month-end close.

How it runs

  • Pull completed services, package redemptions, retail lines, discounts and refunds from the salon software and POS every night.
  • Apply the written commission plan: rates by service category, treatment of discounts, redos and package value, and targets or slabs.
  • Use service values net of GST, so commission is calculated on the salon's revenue rather than on tax collected.
  • Give each stylist or therapist a private running statement with the line items behind it.
  • Let staff raise a query on any line, which goes to the manager with the bill attached.
  • At month end, produce a payout sheet for owner approval and export it to payroll or accounting.

Human checkpoint

The owner or HR lead approves the commission plan, every manual adjustment and the final payout sheet. The manager resolves queries against the original bill. The automation calculates; it never changes pay rules or pays anyone on its own.

Train, track and engageStarter2–3 weeks

Aftercare notes and consented product suggestions

Send each client the stylist's or therapist's own aftercare notes and the products they actually recommended at the visit, with consent, and track retail follow-through without generic promotional blasts.

Salons & spas

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Clients forget aftercare advice by the time they get home, and retail suggestions depend on who was on shift. Generic product blasts feel pushy, AI-generated skin or scalp diagnoses would overstep what a salon should claim, and product claims copied from brand material can break advertising rules.

Trigger

A service is closed in the salon software with aftercare notes or recommended products on the client card.

How it runs

  • The stylist or therapist selects aftercare notes and a few recommended products on the service card before checkout.
  • After the visit, send the aftercare notes, and add the product list only for clients who said yes to product suggestions.
  • Use approved product descriptions only, without medical, cure or promised-result claims.
  • Offer the products through the salon's own store link or for pickup at the next visit.
  • Ask a short feedback question after an agreed period and route any reported irritation or reaction to the manager.
  • Report retail attach rate and follow-through by stylist and service.

Human checkpoint

Stylists and therapists choose every recommendation themselves; AI only tidies the wording of their notes. Any client reporting irritation, a burn or a reaction is called by the manager and advised to seek medical advice.

Renew, rebook or pauseStarter2–3 weeks

Service-based rebooking reminders

Remind each client when their next service is due, based on the service they had and the interval their stylist recommends, with a one-tap link to book the same stylist.

Salons & spas

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Clients who leave without booking their next visit often drift, and a root touch-up, keratin refresh, beard trim, facial or nail infill each has its own natural interval. Front desks cannot track that for hundreds of clients, and generic monthly offers ignore when each person is actually due.

Trigger

A completed service in the salon software, plus a daily check for clients reaching their recommended interval without a future booking.

How it runs

  • Set default rebooking intervals per service with the salon, which stylists can adjust on each client card.
  • At checkout, prompt the receptionist to offer the next appointment before the client leaves.
  • For clients without a future booking, send an approved reminder near the due date with the stylist's next open slots.
  • If the usual stylist has left or is on leave, offer an equally trained colleague without explaining why.
  • Stop after one follow-up, and move clients well past their interval to an occasional consented check-in.

Human checkpoint

Stylists set or change the interval for each client. The salon manager approves the default intervals and the reminder wording. Any offer or discount in a reminder needs manager approval.

Review, refer and returnStarter2–4 weeks

Feedback, review invitations and referral program

Ask every client for private feedback after a visit or milestone, invite everyone to review the same way, route problems to a manager, and run a referral program whose rewards are never tied to reviews.

Gyms & fitness studios · Salons & spas · Yoga & wellness centres · Nutrition & online coaching

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Google reviews drive local discovery for gyms, salons and studios, and referrals drive many coaching sign-ups. But review requests are ad hoc, staff are sometimes told to ask clients to name them or to hit a review count, and referral rewards are tracked by hand. Incentives and asking only happy clients break Google's review rules, and quotas push staff toward both.

Trigger

A completed visit, a milestone such as the first month of membership, the end of a PT package or program, or a client sharing a referral link.

How it runs

  • Send a short private feedback form after the visit or milestone.
  • Open a recovery task for the manager on low scores, with the visit details, so the client hears from a person.
  • Send every client the same review invitation regardless of their score, with no incentive and no request to name staff.
  • Draft replies to new public reviews with AI from approved facts, for the manager to edit and approve.
  • Give each member a personal referral link; rewards apply only when the referred person joins, under published terms, and never depend on a review.
  • Report feedback themes, review coverage and referral joins by location and team.

Human checkpoint

The manager handles every low score personally and approves every public reply, refund or goodwill gesture. Referral rewards beyond the published terms need owner approval. Staff are never given review quotas.
